lore_anchors.definition: A cultivator authorized to carry out sect orders, such as extraditions and assassinations, serving as the cultivation world’s equivalent of internal affairs or a hired enforcer.
An honorific title for a powerful founder of the Azure Sun Sect, referencing "Three Yang" from Daoist alchemy; "Old Devil" here ironically inverts a monk’s honorific into a sign of ruthless power.
The third major cultivation realm, where a cultivator compresses their foundation into a Golden Core, greatly increasing lifespan, power, and the ability to wield high-grade treasures.
A rare, high-powered secret treasure of the Azure Sun Sect, noted for its devastating explosive force; likely derived from compressed Yang thunder energy.

A spiritually barren, low-qi island used as a hiding spot; it draws no attention from passing cultivators, making it a perfect survival hideout in the Mortal Stream logic of valuing camouflage over comfort.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Han Li hesitate to rescue Yuan Yao?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He’s not driven by chivalry—he operates on a “never lift a finger without benefit” principle. He recognizes a chance to extract a rare debt or treasure from a dangerous woman, but only if it is safe to do so.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does the Azure Sun Sect hire outsiders for this mission?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Their founding ancestor (Three Yang Old Devil) is busy, and Yuan Yao is a Core Formation cultivator with stolen sect treasures. They need several Core Formation fighters to ensure a capture, not just a kill.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What is the point of the broken teleportation array scene?
cultural_notes_faq.a: It hints that the protagonist’s journey is being subtly influenced by unseen forces (a common Mortal Stream trope), or simply serves as a humorous delay to show that the world does not always cooperate.
